questions.question: What are passive railroad crossings?

options.text: They have flashing lights.
They have no traffic control devices.
They have gates that lower when trains approach.
Commercial trucks should never cross them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have no traffic control devices.
questions.explanation: Passive crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver must decide when it is safe to cross.

questions.question: How much liquid cargo can be loaded into a tank?

options.text: It depends on the time of year.
It depends on legal weight limits.
It depends on the driver's ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on legal weight limits.
questions.explanation: The amount of liquid you can load depends on how much it will expand during transport, its weight, and legal weight limits. Do not exceed legal weight limits, especially with dense liquids.

questions.question: When driving an empty hazmat tank, what must you do at railroad crossings?

options.text: You can cross without slowing or stopping.
You must slow down but do not have to stop.
You must stop before crossing.
You should never drive over railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop before crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always stop at railroad crossings before crossing, even if the hazmat tank is empty.

questions.question: When using mirrors while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Look quickly.
Look for a long time.
Use only the rearview mirror.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look quickly.
questions.explanation: Looking at mirrors for too long is dangerous. You will travel a long distance without watching the road ahead.

questions.question: Is texting while driving a commercial vehicle allowed?

options.text: Yes, if the text is work-related.
Yes, if the message has fewer than 10 words.
Yes, because it is safer than talking on the phone.
No, it is prohibited.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is prohibited.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving a commercial vehicle is illegal and dangerous. This includes typing or reading any text on an electronic device.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Pass vehicles that are below the speed limit.
Change your driving to match the conditions.
Drive on the shoulder.
Speed up and slow down often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your driving to match the conditions.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly and smoothly on slippery roads. Do not pass slower vehicles unless necessary. Avoid changing your speed frequently.

questions.question: What should you do if a train is approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Try to cross quickly.
Drive around the lowered gates.
Stop and wait for the train to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
questions.explanation: Never try to cross before a train. It is hard to judge how fast a train is moving. If a train is approaching, stop and wait for it to pass before crossing.

questions.question: In bad weather, what do many drivers do?

options.text: They drive in front of trucks.
They drive to the sides of trucks.
They follow trucks too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: They follow trucks too closely.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, many drivers follow large trucks too closely, especially when visibility is poor.

questions.question: Who is responsible for marking and labeling hazardous materials for shipping?

options.text: The mechanic
The shipper
The driver

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for correctly labeling and marking hazardous materials. The driver should check that the shipper did this correctly before starting the trip.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a crash?

options.text: Braking is always the best option.
Swerving may work better than braking.
Keep 100 yards between your vehicle and the next.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may work better than braking.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest choice. You can almost always turn to avoid an obstacle faster than you can stop.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Assume the driver does not see you.
Honk your horn.
Wait for the driver to signal that it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians do not see you when you pass them. This keeps you safe.

questions.question: If you think the road might be icy, you can:

options.text: Guess.
Open your window and touch the side mirror to check for ice.
Look closely at the road.
Check a weather forecast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open your window and touch the side mirror to check for ice.
questions.explanation: Open your window and feel the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna for ice. If ice is on these items, the road is likely icy too.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle usually requires ____ driving a single vehicle.

options.text: Less skill than
About the same skill as
More skill than
The exact same skill as

questions.correctAnswerText: More skill than
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and heavier than single vehicles. They need more skill to drive and are more likely to roll over.

questions.question: What might show that a shipment has hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo comes from a supermarket.
The cargo is in cardboard boxes.
The cargo has green packaging.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often hold hazardous materials. Use proper safety steps when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: Liquid surge happens in:

options.text: Overfilled tanks.
Partially-filled tanks.
Empty tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partially-filled tanks.
questions.explanation: Liquids move back and forth inside partially-filled tanks. Tank drivers must know how surge affects how their vehicle handles.

questions.question: Tanks have high centers of gravity, which means:

options.text: They get very good gas mileage.
They roll over easily.
They are very stable.
They are easy to steer.

questions.correctAnswerText: They roll over easily.
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles have high centers of gravity. This makes them likely to roll over.

questions.question: Why must drivers inspect their vehicles?

options.text: It is usually company policy.
It is usually a local rule.
It is required by federal and state law.
It increases the time they get paid for.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is required by federal and state law.
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to check their vehicles before driving to make sure they are safe to use.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Is not available for most trucks.
Is not useful in most situations.
Is required on newer trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on newer trucks.
questions.explanation: Starting between 1997 and 1999, most commercial vehicles, trailers, and dollies must have ABS.

questions.question: To test the trailer service brakes, you should:

options.text: Move forward slowly and use the brake pedal.
Reverse slowly and use the hand control.
Reverse slowly and use the brake pedal.
Move forward slowly and use the hand control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward slowly and use the hand control.
questions.explanation: First check that air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Then move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control. If the brakes work, you will feel them activate.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep driving and finish the trip.
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Safely pull off the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely pull off the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Stop and sleep if you feel drowsy while driving. Tired drivers cause many fatal accidents.
